description:
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says his country is on the path to an agreement with the US.
Both sides have been holding negotiations over Iran's nuclear programme in Geneva against the backdrop of increased military pressure. 
Araghchi and US envoy Steve Witkoff attended the talks, mediated by Oman. 
Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened military action, first over Iran's deadly crackdown on antigovernment protests and more recently, over its nuclear programme.
Araghchi spoke just after those talks concluded in a positive tone.  

Al Jazeera correspondents are covering the latest developments:
Osama Bin Javaid is in Geneva, Tohid Asadi is in Tehran and Kimberly Halkett is standing by at the White House.

description:
Iranian and US officials have held a second round of nuclear talks in Geneva, which have just concluded.  
Iran's foreign minister had said he wanted to achieve a "fair and equitable deal". 
Donald Trump has repeatedly threatened military action against Iran, first over its violent crackdown on antigovernment protests and more recently, over its nuclear programme.
Iran's supreme leader gave an address while the talks were underway, taking aim at President Trump.

Al Jazeera's Osama bin Javaid has the latest developments from Geneva. 

Ali Vaez, the Iran project director at the International Crisis Group, says Iran talks could have ended because “the gaps are simply too large to bridge” or negotiators didn’t have patience.
